name: Buffalo Grove
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Buffalo Grove, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Buffalo Grove, IL: a kids-only holiday shop, free holiday concerts at Saint Mary Parish and winter break fun at the Raupp Museum.
lede: Buffalo Grove celebrates Christmas through its park district and a historic church: a kids-only holiday shop at the Alcott Center, free concerts and carol sing-alongs at Saint Mary Parish, and holiday traditions from around the world at the Raupp Museum.
celebrates: Christmas in Buffalo Grove is run mostly by the Buffalo Grove Park District. Children do their own gift shopping at the Just For Kids Holiday Shop in the Alcott Center, where holiday helpers guide them and every gift comes wrapped. Santa also has a mailbox at the park district and answers letters from Buffalo Grove kids. For music, BG Singers Encore sings Holiday Harmonies at the Scott Jacobson Community Arts Center, the Buffalo Grove Symphonic Band plays its free holiday concert with audience sing-alongs at Saint Mary Parish, and the Raupp Museum leads a carol sing-along there with the church's 1904 pipe organ. Over winter break, the museum hosts free walk-in afternoons about holidays around the world.
lastyear: In December 2025, the Buffalo Grove Symphonic Band played its holiday concert and posted the full video online. The program opened with Festival Fanfare for Christmas and included Sleigh Ride, a Christmas sing-along, a Christmas pop sing-along, the dreidel song S'Vivon, Yes, Virginia, There is a Santa Claus and the Hallelujah Chorus. BG Singers Encore also took Holiday Harmonies on the road: a family concert with Sleigh Ride, Let It Snow and Let There Be Peace on Earth was planned for December 7, 2025, at the Prospect Heights Public Library.
facts: Local tradition says Buffalo Grove got its name from buffalo that rested at noon under a grove of trees beside Buffalo Creek, or from a buffalo skeleton found by the creek. The first Mass in Buffalo Grove was said in the fall of 1847 in a settler's blockhouse. Saint Mary's chapel, with its landmark steeple, went up in 1899, and its one-manual pipe organ from Slinger, Wisconsin, arrived in 1904 at a cost of $1,300. When the parish opened a new chapel in the 1960s, its very first use was on Christmas Day of 1965.
trains: Buffalo Grove's Metra station sits at 825 Commerce Court on the North Central Service, the line that runs between Union Station and Antioch. The station is accessible, the waiting room is open 5 am to 8 pm, and there is no ticket machine, so riders buy tickets on board or in the Ventra app. Metra's decorated Holiday Trains run on other lines, such as the Milwaukee District North and UP Northwest, rather than the North Central Service. The Illinois Railway Museum in Union runs the Happy Holiday Railway, a ride with Santa and his elves through the winter countryside.

kidfact: Legend says buffalo once walked from the Wheeling woods to rest under a grove of trees by Buffalo Creek every day at noon. That is one story of how Buffalo Grove got its name.
faq: Is there a holiday shop for kids in Buffalo Grove?

Yes. The Buffalo Grove Park District runs the Just For Kids Holiday Shop at the Alcott Center, 530 Bernard Drive, on two evenings in early December. Children shop on their own with the help of holiday helpers, gifts cost $3 to $8, and each present is wrapped and ready to go when they finish.
Can kids write to Santa in Buffalo Grove?

Yes. Santa's Mailbox is a Buffalo Grove Park District tradition for in-district residents. Children mail letters to Santa Claus, care of the Buffalo Grove Park District, 530 Bernard Drive, with a self-addressed stamped envelope, and Santa's helper answers each one. Letters must arrive by the early December deadline printed in the winter guide.
Where can families hear free holiday music in Buffalo Grove?

Saint Mary Parish at 10 N. Buffalo Grove Road hosts two. The Buffalo Grove Symphonic Band plays an annual free holiday concert there with audience sing-alongs, and the Raupp Museum leads a free carol sing-along with the church's 1904 pipe organ, which needs advance registration. Afterward, families can climb to the choir loft to see the organ.

The Raupp Museum at 901 Dunham Lane is the Buffalo Grove Park District's history museum, and admission is free. Kids can sit on the porch of an 1890s farmhouse, milk a replica dairy cow, try a typewriter and peek into an old-fashioned general store. Over winter break it runs free walk-in afternoons on holidays around the world.
Which Metra station serves Buffalo Grove?

The Buffalo Grove station at 825 Commerce Court is on Metra's North Central Service between Union Station and Antioch. The station is accessible and has no ticket machine, so riders buy tickets on board or through the Ventra app. Pace bus routes 234, 272 and 626 connect at the station.
